candidate_flutter.evidence_scope: Declared by immutable Flutter source checked by sibling reviewer; no Gradle resolution or lock/runtime proof performed

decision_reason: Public excludeProperties is real and removes many final property keys, but the available public path does not suppress the unconditional opt-in event or remove the separately attached session metadata envelope. The approved event/property contract was not enlarged to obtain a pass.

findings.claim: optOutTracking publicly documents deletion of unflushed events and People updates. It posts EMPTY_QUEUES; worker deletes events/people/groups/anonymous_people rows by token. This differs materially from PostHog reset preserving the outbound queue.

API returns after posting to Handler; there is no combined deletion/consent completion. Four deletes are separate; opt-out flag is written late and preferences use apply. Crash or a prior flush may precede deletion. hasOptedOutTracking true does not prove purge.

optOutTrackingDefault=true is applied only if already opted out or no flag exists; it does not override a previously saved opt-in. Conversely default=false does not clear a persisted true flag. Existing singleton retrieval does not reconfigure it.
Constructor applies options.serverURL before AnalyticsMessages creation. This supports a future local receiver experiment but does not itself attest zero cloud requests.

MixpanelOptions.Builder.excludeProperties is a supported exact-key exclusion set. Worker merges default/device and caller properties, then applies exclusion before storing/sending. It is not a fail-closed final-payload allowlist hook.

Exclusion skips token,time,distinct_id,$device_id,$user_id,$had_persisted_distinct_id. Default device ID is persisted, but public deviceIdProvider/caller property overrides exist: this review does not claim a real persistent device identity is unavoidable. Additional protocol keys would still need existing-contract approval rather than silent acceptance.

Worker attaches top-level $mp_metadata after applying exclusions to properties. SessionMetadata contains $mp_event_id, $mp_session_id, $mp_session_seq_id, $mp_session_start_sec. Metadata state is private final and no public replacement/disable method was found in the inspected API/options/config. These technical event/session IDs are not classified here as human identifiers; they are extra unapproved session structure under the current contract.

Every optInTracking overload reaches track($opt_in,properties). The public track overload uses isAutomaticEvent=false, so trackAutomaticEvents=false does not suppress it. No public enable-without-event or event-name drop hook was found. identify may additionally emit $identify.

EventBridge receives a prepared properties copy and is notified independently; the event is already prepared for insertion. It has no final-envelope veto contract. ProxyServerInteractor offers headers/response handling, not a final serialized payload mutation/drop hook.

Automatic mobile events can be disabled and autocapture is opt-in; these controls do not remove $opt_in or session envelope. Optional People identity would also cause deleteUser/clearCharges during opt-out and is unnecessary for this lab.

public_alternatives_checked: Direct native MixpanelOptions.excludeProperties exists even though Flutter binding does not expose it; still cannot remove envelope metadata or opt-in event
deviceIdProvider is public and can supply synthetic identity; does not establish full event/payload compliance
reset explicitly leaves already queued analytics messages and flushes; not a consent-enabling substitute
Initialization defaults and a new instance configuration are not a supported reset of previously persisted consent for the same run
No reflection, subclass interception, custom transport, proxy rewrite, internal database deletion or event contract expansion adopted

interruption_test_if_future_supported_ca.acceptance: Do not equate API return or stored opt-out flag with durable deletion. A future candidate requires deterministic interruptions around durable app deny/pending state, SDK delete dispatch, actual deletion completion, and online restart; reconcile all forbidden/new IDs and unrelated sentinels.
static_risks: EMPTY_QUEUES is an in-memory worker message and can be lost before execution
Process death may occur between per-table deletes
Persisted opt-in can survive before async deny write completes
Deny may persist while queue deletion has not completed
A scheduled or in-progress flush can precede EMPTY_QUEUES; no cancellation completion is exposed

limits: Static review only; no runtime result or universally impossible statement
Android source fixed to declared dependency version, not a newly resolved compiled dependency
Twelve selected official source blobs verified against Git tree hashes; full repository/API history not exhaustively audited
No claim that technical session IDs are inherently personal identifiers
No proof that unrelated app data is preserved until future sentinel execution
A public asynchronous deletion API is a testable candidate, not automatically disqualified solely for lacking an ACK; current stop is the separate minimization contract failure
